in_arabic.name: آئیلا
in_arabic.meaning: اسم آئیلا معنی ہے ہالہ یا نشانی۔
in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم آئیلا جو عربی زبان سے ماخوذ ہے، معنی ہے ہالہ یا نشانی۔ یہ نام قرآن مجید میں ذکر ہوا ہے، اور اس کا تعلق علامت یا نشانی سے ہے۔ اسلامی روایت میں، یہ نام اہل ایمان کے لیے ایک शुभ علامت تصور کیا جاتا ہے۔

in_urdu.name: آئیلا

in_urdu.long_meaning: آئیلا نام عربی زبان سے لیا گیا ہے، جس کا مطلب ہے ہالہ یا علامت۔ یہ نام جنوبی ایشیائی مسلم معاشرے میں روایتی اور مذہبی اہمیت رکھتا ہے۔ آئیلا نام کی اصیل عربی جڑوں کو دیکھتے ہوئے، یہ نام اسلامی ثقافت میں علامت یا ہالہ کے طور پر استعمال ہوتا ہے۔

historical_references.reference: According to Arabic mythology, Aiyla was a jinni (genie) woman who fell in love with a human, Al-Harith ibn Kaladah, and bore him a son named Qaladah. Aiyla's love for Al-Harith was so strong that she helped him in his battles and protected him from harm. Eventually, her love was discovered by her jinn community who were enraged and cast her out. She was forced to live among humans, and her son Qaladah was raised by Al-Harith. This story is said to have occurred during the pre-Islamic era, before the advent of Islam in the Arabian Peninsula.

Aiyla was also the name of a notable wife of the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) during his early years in Mecca. She was the sister of Abu Bakr, the first caliph of Islam, and was one of the first converts to Islam. She was known for her devotion and support for her husband during the early stages of Islam, and was a source of comfort and encouragement to the Prophet during difficult times. Aiyla is mentioned in several hadiths (sayings of the Prophet) and is considered an important figure in early Islamic history.
